correctness.rationale: For β=s³(1−s), E_s=3s/2−s², so r⁴−2r³+2E_s r²−β factors as (r−s)²(r²−2(1−s)r−s(1−s)). The roots are L,N in the claim, with N<0<L<r_m<s. The component on the left of s is invariant by energy conservation and contains the well; puncturing it at the equilibrium to speak literally of the period annulus makes no area or probability difference. The interval shrinks with β and the envelope derivative of E_s−V_β(r) is 1/(2s²)−1/(2r²)<0 on it. With r=L+(s−L)t the width times dr is 2(s−L)^(5/2)(1−t)√t·√(r−N)/r dt, differentiable under integration at every interior parameter. The zero-parameter width is bounded by 2(1−r) on (0,1) and tends pointwise to it, giving area 1. Independently using the exact factorization at the fold, with a=3/4 and h=s−a, δ=(9/8)h²+2h³+h⁴, L=a−2h+O(h²), and N→−1/4. Thus h/√δ→c and at r=a+hz the momentum half-height divided by h^(3/2) tends to (4/3)(1−z)√(z+2). Using √(2C)=(4/3)√3·c^(3/2) gives precisely the proposed scaled lobe. Its bounding graphs and endpoints converge with common compact support and a zero-area limiting boundary, yielding L¹ indicator convergence and hence TV convergence after normalization. The area is 24/5 in scaled coordinates, and multiplying by the Jacobian gives 256·2^(3/4)/45 as claimed. Divergence zero gives canonical area invariance; integrating the limiting vertical width and putting w=(z+2)/3 yields density (15/4)√w(1−w). This proof does not require executing the supplied finite checker.
